extracted.intended_audience: ACUS members, consultants, staff, and stakeholders involved in producing or understanding Administrative Conference recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance describing how the Administrative Conference of the United States develops, reviews, adopts, and implements recommendations or occasional Statements about administrative and regulatory processes. Covers roles (Office of the Chairman, consultants, committees, Council, Assembly), report requirements, and adoption/implementation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function: convene public and private sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This purpose frames all recommendation activity: studies and recommendations should aim to improve administrative and regulatory processes through stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage consultants (with Council approval) to study processes needing improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of ACUS’s Council, engages consultants to study particular administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement of external consultants requires Council approval and is the typical mechanism for initiating studies that may lead to recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report accompanied by suggested recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants then prepare a comprehensive research report accompanied by suggested recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be comprehensive in scope and include concrete suggested recommendations as the basis for deliberation and adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house report preparation as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, ACUS staff members prepare these reports in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, staff-produced reports may substitute for consultant reports; such reports should likewise be comprehensive and include suggested recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive deliberation by committees prior to adoption for Council consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: After extensive deliberation, committees of ACUS’s voting and non-voting members adopt proposed recommendations for Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee deliberation is expected to be thorough and involve both voting and non-voting members before proposals advance to the Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council consideration and forwarding with its views
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council then forwards the recommendations, with its views, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council not only transmits recommendations but also records and forwards its institutional views to inform Assembly debate and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly debate, amendment, and formal adoption (typically semi-annually in plenary session)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly typically meets semi-annually in plenary session to debate, amend, and formally adopt the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption commonly occurs in semi-annual plenary Assembly sessions where debate and amendment are expected parts of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACUS undertakes to implement adopted recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS then undertakes to implement them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following formal adoption, ACUS is responsible for undertaking implementation activities to effect the adopted improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of 'Statements' as an alternative output
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the Conference membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements are typically produced by the same process as recommendations but may present issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than formal recommendations; they are included in the searchable database of recommendations.
